english: For a real number $\lambda$, consider the system of linear equations
in the unknowns $x,y,z$. Then the set of all values of $\lambda$ for which the system has a non-trivial solution is
hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $\lambda$ के लिए अज्ञात $x,y,z$ में रैखिक समीकरण निकाय
पर विचार कीजिए। तब $\lambda$ के उन सभी मानों का समुच्चय, जिनके लिए निकाय का एक अतुच्छ (non-trivial) हल है, होगा
solution: Homogeneous form $(C-\lambda I)X=O$ with $C=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\\3&6&9\end{pmatrix}$; non-trivial solution $\iff\det(C-\lambda I)=0$
Rows of $C$ are proportional, so every $2\times2$ minor and $\det C$ are $0$; $\mathrm{tr}\,C=14$
($\lambda=0$ must be kept: then all three equations are $x+2y+3z=0$, which has non-trivial solutions)
solution_full: Moving the right sides to the left, the system is $(1-\lambda)x+2y+3z=0$, $2x+(4-\lambda)y+6z=0$, $3x+6y+(9-\lambda)z=0$, a homogeneous system $(C-\lambda I)X=O$ with $C=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\\3&6&9\end{pmatrix}$.
A homogeneous square system has a non-trivial solution exactly when its coefficient determinant is $0$.
Expanding, $\det(C-\lambda I)=-\lambda^{3}+(\mathrm{tr}\,C)\lambda^{2}-m\lambda+\det C$, where $m$ is the sum of the three $2\times2$ principal minors of $C$.
Each row of $C$ is a multiple of $(1,2,3)$, so every $2\times2$ minor is $0$ (for example $1\cdot4-2\cdot2=0$, $1\cdot9-3\cdot3=0$, $4\cdot9-6\cdot6=0$) and $\det C=0$.
So the determinant vanishes only for $\lambda=0$ and $\lambda=14$.
Check $\lambda=0$: every equation reduces to $x+2y+3z=0$, which has non-trivial solutions such as $(2,-1,0)$.
originality_note: New: the coefficient matrix is lambda I minus a rank-one matrix with rows in ratio 1:2:3, so the determinant collapses to lambda^2(14 - lambda) and the double root lambda = 0 is the trap (way 4). Closest known: 'x + lambda y - z = 0, lambda x - y - z = 0, ... has a non-trivial solution for'. Different because: the rank-one structure gives a repeated root that students drop.
blueprint_concepts: Homogeneous system AX = 0: condition for non-trivial solutions

concept_use.Homogeneous system AX = 0: condition for: The system is rewritten as (C - lambda I)X = O and a non-trivial solution exists iff det(C - lambda I) = 0, which gives lambda^2(14 - lambda) = 0.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy factorises det(C - lambda I) = -lambda^2(lambda - 14); the null spaces at lambda = 0 and 14 are non-zero. Changed: stated that x, y, z are the unknowns and lambda is real.
key_step: Recognising that det(C - lambda I) = lambda^2(14 - lambda) because C has rank one, and keeping lambda = 0.
justification: Single concept but a three-step chain (rewrite as homogeneous, determinant, factor with the repeated root); above the direct consistency matching of 2023-P1-Q14 (L1) and at the routine-chain level of 2026-P2-Q1 (L2).
